💡 Key Takeaways
  • Following last week‘s PlayStation 5 and PC pre-order launch, Switch 2 and Switch digital pre-orders for Professor Layton and the Upcoming World of Steam are now available for $64.99 / £53.99 / €64.99 / ¥7,920, LEVEL-5 announced.
  • Industry observers note that as previously declared, pre-orders include the “Layton Series Soundtrack Selection,” a digital soundtrack featuring 11 pieces of music from the Professor Layton series.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following last week‘s PlayStation 5 and PC pre-order launch, Switch 2 and Switch digital pre-orders for Professor Layton and the Upcoming World of Steam are now available for $64.99 / £53.99 / €64.99 / ¥7,920, LEVEL-5 announced. The official website has also been updated with story and gameplay information.

Industry observers note that as previously declared, pre-orders include the “Layton Series Soundtrack Selection,” a digital soundtrack featuring 11 pieces of music from the Professor Layton series. The tracks are accessible via the “Secret Content” menu in-game.

This latest adventure takes place one year after the events of Professor Layton and the Unwound Future.

The story unfolds in America, where the Wild West era has ended and the country is forging ahead into a new age of development.

A letter from Luke leads Layton to Steam Bison, a town renowned for its inventions….

Sources indicate that steam Bison has undergone rapid technological advances thanks to the steam engine. But mysterious events are unfolding one after another, from a phantom gunman who has kidnapped a wealthy heiress to a gang of zombies threatening the town. Layton and Luke join forces once again to investigate these strange occurrences and embark on a grand puzzle-solving adventure.

◆ A Story That Unfolds as You Solve Puzzles.

You’ll encounter all kinds of puzzles as you explore the streets of Steam Bison.

—Even to meet Eggmuffin, an inventor, you’ll need to solve a puzzle to find the entrance to his room….

—Solve the puzzle, and the story moves forward.

◆ The Most Puzzles in Series History.

Industry observers note that layton and Luke face more puzzles than ever before in the series. Solve a wide variety of puzzles as you progress through the story and get to the bottom of the mysterious events unfolding in Steam Bison. Along the way, you’ll even come across puzzles that play a part in Steam Bison’s development. Solve them to upgrade the town’s facilities and watch the town flourish.

—Solve puzzles to develop facilities!

Sources indicate that what’s more, a new puzzle will be added to Daily Puzzles every day for over a year following launch. This lets you enjoy the game long after you’ve completed the story.

Whether you prefer to take your time solving puzzles on your own or gather around a big screen with family and friends to work them out together, that’s all part of the fun of the Layton series.

According to recent reports, stand Use snippets of conversation between café customers to recreate the drinks they ordered. Get the drinks right, and you might hear some juicy local gossip!

It has been revealed that use a mysterious device to transform ordinary items into treasure. Master its three modes: Reversal, Evolution, and Fusion!

Recent findings suggest that the duck robot that monitors the factory won’t stop once it’s set in motion! Give it the right commands to overcome obstacles and complete the operational test.

In a recent development, experience Professor Layton and the Fresh World of Steam in different languages! Choose your preferred languages for text and voice, and set off on an adventure with Professor Layton and Luke! Mix and match languages to experience the story in a whole new way!

Explore the Professor Layton games in the order their stories take place.

Professor Layton and the New World of Steam is due out for PlayStation 5, Switch 2, Switch, and PC via Steam on December 10.

View screenshots of the game in additional languages at the gallery.

AMD's next-gen Zen 6 desktop CPUs are rumoured to be delayed, may be pushed back to second half of 2027

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (522 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We got our first technical deep dive into AMD's next-generation Zen 6 CPU architecture last week, in the form of the tech giant's new Venice range of server chips.
  • Sources indicate that the upcoming Ryzen offerings were originally thought to be launching in the first half, but Chiphell leaker Zhang Zhonghao notes otherwise.
  • Zhang Zhonghao makes mention of Computex in their post, which some are speculating means a launch date after the show in June of next year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We got our first technical deep dive into AMD's next-generation Zen 6 CPU architecture last week, in the form of the tech giant's new Venice range of server chips. Now there's a rumour that the consumer Ryzen chip launch may have been pushed back to the second half of 2027.

Sources indicate that the upcoming Ryzen offerings were originally thought to be launching in the first half, but Chiphell leaker Zhang Zhonghao notes otherwise. In a post spotted by Videocardz, Zhang Zhonghao claims that the desktop chips, codenamed Olympic Ridge, have been switched to TSMC's N2X manufacturing process, and as a result the "timeline has been pushed back" (via machine translation).

Zhang Zhonghao makes mention of Computex in their post, which some are speculating means a launch date after the show in June of next year.

Olympic Ridge was originally though to be using TSMC's N2 or N2P process node, but a switch to the performance-focussed N2X would line up with previous rumours that the chips are targeting very high clockspeeds, potentially all the way up to 6.5 GHz.

Industry observers note that N2X is scheduled to enter production in 2027, which would explain the longer timeframe if this rumour proves out. A delay to the second half of next year would mean that Intel's Nova Lake chips, mentioned by the organization to be "tracking ahead of schedule" in a recent earnings call, would potentially have the first half of 2026 all to themselves if they launch before Zen 6.

In the battle of the next generation CPUs, Intel would end up with a significant headstart. However, for those thinking about a potential upgrade, it's worth noting that Intel's newly introduced chips will use an entirely new socket in the form of LGA 1954. AMD's new offerings will use the existing AM5 socket.

AMD's Jack Huynh posted a cryptic video on X earlier this week, alongside a message declaring that "the next era of computing is going to be special," and that he "can't wait to share a glimpse of what's coming at CES." So, hopefully we might learn more about what's going on with Zen 6 desktop silicon on January 5.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

2. Best motherboard: MSI MAG X870 Tomahawk WiFi.

3. Best RAM: G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB 32 GB DDR5-7200.

It has been revealed that 5. Best graphics card: AMD Radeon RX 9070.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again.
  • To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun.
  • Recent findings suggest that it's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'!

Recent findings suggest that I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

Recent findings suggest that it's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - founded by ex-GTA veteran - has a mountain of debt, and the main blueprint for paying it back is litigation

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (557 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the company created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt.
  • This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back.
  • In a recent development, "Prior to the Organization's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the company created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt. And a huge chunk of that appears to be owed to Chinese gaming company NetEase (£36.5m), though more than £1m appears to be owed to Benzies himself.

This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back. And the manufacturer's "largest" potential asset, according to the administrators, is litigation.

In a recent development, "Prior to the Organization's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary.

It has been revealed that "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that any such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions.".

This tallies with the narrative spun by co-company leader Mark Gerhard as the company waded into deep water. Gerhard blamed "organised espionage and corporate sabotage" for the studio's difficulties as multiple rounds of layoffs shredded Build a Rocket Boy. "People had their hands on the scale and deliberately tried to shape a negative narrative around the product," Gerhard said.

In a recent development, the situation he's referring to is likely the alleged smear campaign made against the game, which Gerhand reportedly claimed in an internal meeting this year was paid for by a "significant American company" and then run by a UK company called Ritual Network, which apparently had influencers, journalists and staff at Build a Rocket Boy deliberately sabotage the game's release. That's according to an account of a videoed internal meeting reportedly seen by Insider Gaming earlier this year.

According to recent reports, it had nothing to do with the dire state of Mindseye when it launched, then. Eurogamer awarded it one out of five stars, chastising its "ridiculous story, inconsistent writing, poorly designed mission scenarios, and utterly atrocious combat" in our Mindseye review.

Industry observers note that build a Rocket Boy was founded in 2016, and its first game, Everywhere - a sort of online gaming platform - was announced in 2022. It never materialised, but a part of that vision was carved out to become a standalone game experience of its own along the way, and that's how we got Mindseye - a take on a Grand Theft Auto formula. Whether or not the litigation is successful and can recoup any of Build a Rocket Boy's debts remains to be seen, but there's a financial mountain for the studio to climb if it hopes to operate again.

That Time Robert Pattinson’s The Odyssey Request Was Immediately Shot Down By Christopher Nolan

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (640 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, we know Robert Pattinson is on Christopher Nolan’s “nice list” considering he’s cast the actor in two of his movies.
  • Pattinson, of course, plays the very deplorable Antinous in The Odyssey.
  • I didn't even know how he got my number… The answer was no.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we know Robert Pattinson is on Christopher Nolan’s “nice list” considering he’s cast the actor in two of his movies. (Did you know Pattinson even helped inspire Nolan to make Oppenheimer?) While the pair seem to have a great filmmaking partnership going, there was one time on the set of The Odyssey where Nolan totally rejected one choice Pattinson was hoping for on the spot.

Pattinson, of course, plays the very deplorable Antinous in The Odyssey. Before cameras started rolling, the actor reached out to the hair department to request a long wig for the part. As the movie’s hair department head Gloria Casny told it, when he called she just happened to be standing right next to Nolan. In her words:.

I didn't even know how he got my number… The answer was no.

Sources indicate that that’s right. No conversation or negotiations, just “no”. Casny told the story during a news conference for The Odyssey in promotion of it becoming one of the latest 2026 movies that’s available to watch at home. The story led Matt Damon, who was the event’s moderator, to make this comment:.

It's funny because he knows Chris and he’s worked with Chris… Chris is literally allergic to anything like that.

Recent findings suggest that I can definitely see Pattinson’s vision for Antinous, but apparently one of Nolan’s rules is he doesn’t like to have actors wear any wigs or fake facial hair. Makes sense for the filmmaker who famously tries to do as much of his movies practically as possible.

In a recent development, there’s been a few other stories around Nolan and Pattinson that have also come out before. For example, he’s reportedly the only cast member who asked to read the script. Also, Mia Goth told a story about how one time on set Pattinson approached Nolan with a question while they were filming and Nolan simply responded with “That’s your department, mate”. Nolan has a different way of working than most, but that’s got to be one reason he’s considered one of our best living filmmakers.

Pattinson wasn’t the only actor on the set of The Odyssey that made a request to the hair department. As Matt Damon told USA Today during the same event, he had actually asked Nolan if he could have a fake beard to play Odysseus. Can you guess Nolan’s answer? Per Damon’s words:.

In a recent development, he just looked at me like, 'No.’ He’s like, ‘Just grow your beard.’ He likes everything real. To be fair, given the amount of time spent in the ocean and water alone, the hand-laid beard would never have worked. Where you’re just out in the elements all the time, it just wouldn’t have made sense.

Same reaction! How funny. Damon really did grow a magnificent beard though, so it all worked out. And, honestly Pattinson’s forward-swept bangs fit perfectly, too. You can appreciate the lack of wigs on The Odyssey by purchasing it for home viewing now.

Mondrayn is a putrid, crunchy pixel art RPG about escaping from limbo where "dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering"

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The world of Mondrayn is a dead one.
  • Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

In a recent development, everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates. Instead, it's because of… Elon Musk's mother.

It has been revealed that some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk. The trailer is for a fresh enhancement - dubbed Cicia - which adds the ability to drive futuristic hovering cars. The reveal comes days after a widely mocked demonstration of Musk's own Tesla "flying car", which doesn't actually fly.

While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family.

"If they promote Tesla or mention him in the game I'm 100 percent dropping it," wrote one Reddit user (via The Gamer). "Why would they involve that man in a girly fashion game, and if they wanted a car brand partnership why not a Chinese one??!? Infold is addicted to negative attention I swear.".

It has been revealed that "If Tesla is somehow involved in the design of the car (or worse, an in-game promotion), then I might have to let go," wrote another person in the same thread. "Please please please be wrong.".

Recent findings suggest that though Maye Musk's involvement might seem random, there may be a good explanation for it. "Here's something that might surprise people who only know her as Elon's mother: Maye Musk is a celebrity in China in her own right," Reddit user BarbieSpeedRacer explained.

Industry observers note that "She's a successful model, an author, and a recognisable advertising personality. Her memoir became popular with Chinese readers, and she's appeared in campaigns and promotional events for brands including OPPO, Fila, and JNBY.".

Her image as "a woman in her seventies who continues to work as a fashion model" is one that resonates with the game's Chinese audience, apparently, especially "among women interested in fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content".

"A Chinese company makes an advertisement featuring a celebrity popular in China, and an international fandom interprets that decision almost exclusively through the lens of American domestic politics," the post added.

Sources indicate that so far, calls for a boycott don't appear to have coalesced into a movement, at least judging by the game's subreddit. Even if Western players were to organise one, it's not likely to hurt Infinity Nikki much, as most of the game's revenue - estimated at more than 80 percent - comes from Chinese players.

In Eurogamer's Infinity Nikki review, Jessica Orr noted it advances the genre of open-world gacha games and brings competition to rival developer miHoYo, writing: "The changes in length, combat and progression all feel utterly invigorating compared to other Genshin-likes, and it's why Infinity Nikki feels like it could (and should) be on the same trajectory to shake up the gacha scene just like Genshin Impact did in 2020.".

On by default, game captures automatically uploaded to Xbox Live servers are scanned for offensive imagery, including hate speech, drugs misuse, excessive violence, as well as nudity and sexual content.

According to recent reports, according to some Reddit sleuthing, GTA 6 players are being banned for uploading content captured on the beach in Leonida amongst other activities. Sources indicate that if you think about it, it would be odd to walk around a beach with a video camera filming the locals, but it's a bit silly to see Xbox players getting 2-day bans. The rulings appear to be automated and unappealable too.

In a recent development, it's not clear if sexual content or nudity is the cause for the violation, but it's worth noting GTA 6 does contain full-frontal nudity. We'd recommend not spamming the capture button during those sequences. Xbox doesn't like that sort of thirsty behaviour.

It's been a huge year for the games industry with all sorts of heavy-hitters releasing over the past few months, and as we look towards the end of 2026, we're now checking in on Metacritic's highest-rated games of the year based on the user score.

While Grand Theft Auto 6 may have officially surpassed Ocarina's Remake as the highest-rated game of 2026 on the review aggregate website (and also matched the original N64 hit as the highest-rated critic Metascore of all time), it seems the classic outing on Switch 2 has won players' hearts worldwide.

Recent findings suggest that according to the latest patch from the site, Ocarina's Remake is presently sitting in the top highest-rated games (above 90), based on user score (it's on 9.2/10 at the time of writing). It's in good organization with other games like Resident Evil Requiem and Splatoon Raiders.

Obviously, there are all sorts of different factors in play here when it comes to user scores (and the system in place isn't necessarily perfect). For example, Ocarina's Remake has over 25,000 user reviews, whereas other titles may have around 100 reviews. Keep in mind, user scores are also subject to change over time.

And if you're wondering how GTA 6 has been received by players, it's currently sitting on a user score of 5.5/10 after more than 30,000 user reviews. Even with supposed review bombings, it might take some time before it wins over some players. Despite top marks from critics, this new entry in the GTA universe appears to have divided the fanbase in its opening week.

As attention shifts towards the end-of-year game awards, both Ocarina and GTA 6 have already been nominated for multiple industry awards.

Is the Ocarina's remake your favourite game this year? Or would you nominate something else? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

Sources indicate that "What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the prepares for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely fresh modes, the possibilities are vast.".

The post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Recent findings suggest that anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a major visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, fresh motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

Recent findings suggest that beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big enhancement sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, knights of the Old Republic is my favorite RPG of all time, and a key reason why my love of video games developed as deeply as it did. My hopes for Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic, a spiritual successor to BioWare's classic, are sky-high, and expectations from the broader community are similarly intense. Director Casey Hudson isn't too worried about that pressure, though – after all, he and much of the team at Arcanaut Studios made the original KOTOR and the Mass Effect trilogy.

"I think it would be really weird to do if I hadn't worked on the first one," Hudson admits in an interview for The Fourth Curtain podcast. "It would feel really strange. But I think, for us, we've got folks on the team who worked on that game and have worked on all the Mass Effect games since and other BioWare stuff.".

Hudson indicates that experience "helps," because the studio knows "why we did things the way we did. We're not trying to fill someone else's shoes, despite the expectations being really high.".

We still know very little about Fate of the Old Republic, other than the fact that it's a spiritual successor to KOTOR. What kind of gameplay systems will it build on? I can't imagine KOTOR's creaky D&D 3.5-based mechanics are going to make a comeback. What kind of story will it tell? It's going to have to be something all-new, with the entire Star Wars universe having been rebooted since KOTOR was new.

According to recent reports, "The thing that supersedes everything is our passion and excitement for doing something amazing," Hudson notes. "That has to outshine everything else, because you can't really know how to answer pressure, and it's hard to even really understand what other people want to play. But if you're so excited about making something that people are going to love, you're just passionate about it being amazing, that leads you to where you want to go.".

That's maybe an obvious answer, but I appreciate that it's the one Hudson is providing. No new game can possibly live up to my nostalgic memories of BioWare's Star Wars RPG, and what I really want is a new game created by a team of people who are excited about what they're making. If it can tap into my old love for KOTOR, that's just icing on the cake.

Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic director Casey Hudson says there'll be "fresh announcements" about the KOTOR successor next year.

#74862. You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (534 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (534 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them.
  • It has been revealed that you can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress.
  • It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them. This might be a shock to some people, since the option to do so was included in Rockstar games as recently as GTA 5, but here once you've made progress in the story, that's it. Our reviewer confirmed this in his 100+ hour playthrough of the title.

It has been revealed that you can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress. By my maths, that means you're going to want to make a fresh manual save for every 6.6 percent of the game you complete. There is, of course, an auto-save slot, too, that should help you out if you get Busted or Wasted. There will also be key story missions - you will be able to tell when they are, much like you could tell when there was about to be a major heist in GTA 5, a showdown in GTA: San Andreas, or a raid on a gang lord's mansion in GTA: Vice City - that you may want to save before attempting.

It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6. "The team embraced more of an open-ended design philosophy on this project," indicates David Hynd, vice president of technology on GTA 6. "For example, we really wanted to reduce the number of Mission fails for the player experimenting or trying something different. And we wanted to encourage the player to do what felt right to them for their particular play style.".

That means that Rockstar, by considering its deployment of standard gameplay mechanics and enemy AI, and re-evaluating how it approached mission and level design, has created "many different ways" for you to approach any given mission in the game. The result? "It's a lot harder to keep Missions as open as possible (especially in a game as large as this), but the freedom and flexibility it allows the player was worth it," states Hynd. He also notes that the team expects players to "learn and reapply" consistent rules in terms of how the world works - and be surprised when they do and don't apply.

Sources indicate that in the previous game, you could access any previous mission you'd completed and be able to play it again on a whim. For GTA 5, you'd simply boot up Story Mode, open the pause menu, go to Game > Replay Mission, and pick the mission you want to play. GTA 6's structure is more complicated, though, hence why Rockstar made the decision to make progress this linear.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 comes out tomorrow. You can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 at the link, and read our 5-star review of the game here. If you want to, ahem, 'travel to Upcoming Zealand' to get ahead of the timezones, it seems the country would be happy to have you.

Ahead of the launch of GTA 6, there was a whole lot of talk online about the Xbox "Upcoming Zealand trick" and how people could get early access to the game by switching their regions to New Zealand on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.

We mentioned in various articles how it was a risky practice (against Xbox's ToCs), but one that had never traditionally resulted in any widespread bans, and it doesn't seem like either Xbox or Rockstar took any action at first glance.

As it turns out, a lot of people decided to give it a go for the upcoming Grand Theft Auto.

This is according to the folks at Ampere Analysis (via The Game Business), who report that over 2.1 million people played GTA 6 in the US and the UK before it was officially released.

As you can see from the graph above, it seems the vast majority of those were based in the United States, followed by the UK, Canada, Brazil and Mexico. Only around 100,000 people tried the trick on PS5 in the U.S. (where it's harder to implement and requires a separate account), whereas 1.5 million of them ended up using it on Xbox.

Recent findings suggest that ultimately, the existence of the New Zealand trick probably led to a bunch of increased sales for Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, but it also poses the question of whether Xbox might be forced to put a stop to it on Project Helix and beyond. As much it's a beloved feature, it's also being used in a way that wasn't originally intended.

Let's see what happens in the future, but for now, it's clearly made a lot of people happy this week!

Did you use the New Zealand trick for GTA 6? Let us know your experiences with it in the comments.

Survivor's coin flip remains a controversial addition to the game, as fans debate the pros and cons of what it brings to the CBS series. I initially didn't have issues with what went down with Lewis Kelly in Season 51's flip, until I learned there was more than one flip involved.

Lewis spoke to Rob Has A Podcast about his exit and was asked if he'd pick water over fire if he flipped the coin again in a future season. The third juror revealed that he didn't have to think about the hypothetical, because he flipped the coin twice the night of his elimination. Hear the story below:.

According to recent reports, well, here's the thing. I did actually do it once [before the one shown] and it didn't land in the circle, and I hear 'fire.' And maybe I should've changed it. I didn't think about it, so, it's tough.

Lewis had to flip the coin twice, and the first time it landed on fire! Unfortunately, because it didn't land primarily in the circle placed on the ground, it was negated and he had to flip it again. Lewis didn't say how he felt about that, but I can say that as a Survivor fan, I'm pissed.

Survivor 51's Kilby Lost All Of His Worldly Possessions After A Wild Storage Wars Scheme Went South.

I went back and watched Survivor, and Jeff Probst mentioned that the contestant who correctly called the coin flip won immunity, an idol, and the grand prize went up another million. The only rule was that it had to land on what he called. At no point was it said the coin had to land on the mat, which wasn't even used for the shot of Lewis' coin flip.

Jeff's word is law on Survivor, and if he's allowed to push contestants to admit they like fire challenges on-camera, he should've honored the result of the initial coin flip. Obviously, they faked it for the camera that he took the flip a second time on camera. They should've stuck with his original flip result and just filmed until he recreated it in the way they wanted it shot.

Recent findings suggest that to me, multiple flips for the coin feel sketchy. Sure, Lewis had a 50/50 shot both times, and one flip didn't impact the outcome of the other. At the same time, Lewis won the first flip and had it negated by something that wasn't part of the rules. Is it then fair that his odds of survival went back to 50% for a redo?

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Now, there's also a third option here in which the mat and all of that was explained to Lewis ahead of the flip, and maybe that's why he wasn't as bent out of shape as I am. I'll also admit he was one of my favorites, so I'm also sad about seeing him head to the jury before this season wraps up on the 2026 TV schedule.

Recent findings suggest that survivor's Open Era continues to be full of surprises, which certainly keeps both the contestants and viewers on their toes. I think the biggest disappointment with this coin flip is that the payoff was pushed to next season. Right now, all we have to fester on is disappointment, and the fact that someone threw away their chance to stay in the game on a coin flip. We'll see what happens next Wednesday, and how Lewis' exit will impact the group dynamic.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you've been online at all today, you'll know that what feels like the entire world is right now fawning over GTA 6. As the reviews dropped, one thing quickly became very clear: this is a game absolutely packed with detail. Our own Chris noted that, thanks to this focus on specific detail and unbelievable nuance, Grand Theft Auto 6 is "the most unbelievable video game world ever made". And it's no accident: this is something Rockstar put a lot of dedicated effort into.

Sources indicate that it's been well-established that the studio has gone above and beyond to make this interactive world one of the most richly-developed we've ever seen: Rockstar has told us it "re-engineered" its weather systems to "achieve a sense of scale we haven't felt before," adding hurricanes, rainbows and heavy rain. It simulated and built a complex drug system, allowing Lucia and Jason to partake in drug use "directly from their inventory" and "at any time". But there are still details emerging from the dev team that are blowing my mind. And the most recent byte of information I saw was related to how Rockstar worked with sound.

"Much of the dynamic soundscape is informed by the incredibly detailed art throughout the world," explains Alastair MacGregor, vice president of audio at Rockstar. "One small example is that convenience store refrigerators all have their own unique sounds. In a run-down store, the refrigerators and freezers are loud and sound like they are badly maintained. Their compressor units can be heard mechanically whirring away from years of neglect. As a result, the bottles behind the doors can be heard shaking and the units click on and off more frequently. In an up-market store, the refrigerators are quieter, adding a subtle hum to the environment.".

This level of detail is, quite frankly, absurd. It's a testament to granularity Rockstar is willing to go to in making Leonida feel truly lived-in and realistic. And this level of production isn't restricted to internal locations, either. "On the ambient side, we love the contrast between the manicured luxury islands, with the sizzle of crickets and lawn sprinklers backed by birdsong, yacht halyards clanging in the distance, and yard work going on, versus urban areas with the sounds of people living on top of each other - snatches of every genre of music, distant voices, cars peeling out, construction, the omnipresent hum of elderly air conditioners struggling with the humidity," continues MacGregor.

Sources indicate that he goes on to say that if you're wandering the streets of Gellhorn - a coastal city in Kelly County on the western side of Leonida - it's acoustically a very different vibe than the high-rise centre of Vice City, where the sound bounces between the buildings. This means that the engine is handling not just the sounds of things as minute as bugs in the grass, but also how that sound travels, and interacts with other physical entities in the world. "We've spent years iterating on reverb technology to make sure that you can feel that - from the pops of cars backfiring to the wash of a helicopter passing by overhead to birds squawking in the trees," concludes MacGregor.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 launches tomorrow - Thursday, 19th November - for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It's also worth noting that Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a dense adventure with many secrets to find, and while the critical path is fairly linear, it's rarely straightforward - asking you to pick up select items and upgrades before you can start exploring its many dungeons.

That's why a Zelda: Ocarina of Time walkthrough comes in handy. Though the Switch 2 version follows the same beats as the N64 original, we'd estimate around 10% of the game's puzzles and locations have been changed or updated - just enough to throw off those very familiar with the 1998 version.

This page features both an abridged and thorough walkthrough covering the critical path, plus a repository of our other Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides, from optional side-quests to items and collectables.

If you want brief directions and as few spoilers as possible in terms of item unlocks and progression, then use the following abridged walkthrough to take you through the game. If you want extra specifics - including useful optional extras as you go - then check the following section.

Sources indicate that for a more detailed walkthrough of the critical path, this section can explain specific steps on how to progress. If you want even more detailed step-by-step guides to the game's many dungeons, then follow the links to dedicated pages on each.

In a recent development, before you can visit the Great Deku Tree, you must find a Sword and Shield, otherwise Mido won’t let you through. You can find the Kokori Sword in the Forest Training Center to the southwest (crawl through the vent to get there, then find it in the chest above), and the Deku Shield from the shop in the northeast by collecting Rupees found scattered around the village.

In a recent development, visit the Deku Tree, complete the Great Deku Tree dungeon, and get the Kokiri’s Emerald key item and an instruction to head to Hyrule Castle. Now leave Kokiri Forest to the west to receive an Ocarina in a cutscene before leaving to Hyrule Field.

In a recent development, head directly north along the path until you reach the castle drawbridge. The area inside is the Hyrule Castle Market - there’s lots of optional activities here, including the chance to get your first Bottle from the Potion Shop - and when ready, proceed to Hyrule Castle, where after getting the Weird Egg from Maron, you must make your way through the grounds to meet Zelda.

Industry observers note that you'll now have Zelda’s Letter and learnt Zelda’s Lullaby on the Ocarina. The critical path is to Death Mountain via Kakariko Village, though you should visit the Lost Woods first (for Saria's Song, which you'll need shortly) and ideally, an optional visit to Lon Lon Ranch (for a Bottle and the first step in how to get Epona).

When ready, go east from Hyrule Field’s drawbridge and up the steps to Kakariko Village.

After finding all Cucco locations for a Bottle and visiting the Graveyard for the Sun’s Song (both optional), show Zelda’s Letter to the guard at the north exit. He gives you an optional errand - returning to the Hyrule Castle Market for a "proper shield" (the Hylian Shield) and also to start the Happy Mask Shop quest.

When ready, head to Death Mountain.

In a recent development, the aim is to reach Goron City. Hug the rightmost wall: this will take you up and round the corner, then back on yourself up the cliff. The path will now split: take the left branch to Goron City.

Inside Goron City, head to the lowest level, where on the north side is a closed door. Play Zelda’s Lullaby here to open it. Inside is Darunia. Talk to him, then play Saria’s Song (which you can get from the Lost Woods). This will see you unlock the Goron’s Bracelet, allowing you to use Bomb Flowers.

It has been revealed that now leave Goron City the way you came (the top entrance), then go directly right to see a Bomb Flower near a fence. Now you have the Goron's Bracelet, throw it over and you’ll bomb the entrance to Dodongo Cavern, allowing you to enter.

Once you have completed the Dodongo Cavern dungeon and picked Bombs and the Goron’s Ruby (the Spiritual Stone of Fire), feel free to scale Death Mountain for a Great Fairy Fountain location (unlocking Din's Fire) before heading off to Zora Domain.

Zora River - which leads to Zora Domain - is just east of Kakariko Village and Death Mountain on Hyrule Field.

Reach the end - the way there is fairly linear - and access Zora Domain by playing Zelda's Lullaby at the waterfall.

Inside, you must find the whereabouts of Princess Ruto by getting the Silver Scale in a mini-game at the top of the waterfall, then by visiting Lake Hylia via the underwater shortcut for a Bottle with a letter inside. (Our dedicated Zora Domain walkthrough features more specific directions for all these, by the way!).

Speak to King Zora, Bottle up a fish found in Zora Domain, then give it to the giant fish in Zora Fountain to access Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly dungeon.

It has been revealed that once the dungeon is complete and the Spiritual Stone of Water is in your possession, head to Hyrule Castle. After the cutscene, dive in the moat and collect the Ocarina of Time, where you’ll then learn the Song of Time.

Sources indicate that head to the Temple of Time which branches off from Hyrule Castle Market. Inside, stand in front of the inscription at the far end, and play the Song of Time. Now go into the next room and retrieve the Master Sword.

Sources indicate that after the cutscene, you’ll become Adult Link, and are told to head to Kakariko Village. Do so, then head to the Graveyard. On the left row of graves is a tombstone with flowers in front; push the stone and head down the hole. Now follow Dampe through the maze and at the end, you’ll receive the Hookshot.

To leave, play the Song of Time on the blocks, to emerge in the Windmill. Use this opportunity to get the Heart Piece opposite, then speak to the man to learn the Song of Storms - you’ll need this later.

With the Hookshot in hand, you can explore more of Hyrule, but when ready, head to Forest Temple: it can be found at the end of the Lost Woods, and inside the dungeon, you'll unlock the Bow and be rewarded with the Forest Medallion story item.

In a recent development, complete the Forest Temple dungeon to unlock a Sage. At this point onward, upon returning to the Temple of Time, you can time travel back into Young Link by putting the Master Sword the pedestal. Also, to help, Sheik will teach you The Prelude of Light, which allows you to teleport back to the Temple of Time - a pretty handy shortcut.

As Adult Link, make your way to Death Mountain (it’s worth going into the Shooting Gallery in Kakariko Village now you have the Bow, which rewards you the Substantial Quiver to hold 40 Rupees as you go), then head into Goron City.

On the next level down is a Goron rolling around, and your aim is to detonate a Bomb near him so he stops. Once successful, the Goron will reveal their name is Link, son of Darunia, and will explain the Goron's plight.

Exhaust the dialogue options to receive the Goron Tunic - a red garb which allows you to withstand high temperatures - and directions to the Fire Temple, which is by heading to Darunia’s room (located on the bottom level at the back) and then by pulling the statue to reveal a route to the Death Mountain Crater.

Sources indicate that once in, go over the drawbridge using the Hookshot to meet Sheik, who will teach you Bolero of Fire. Now head through the left doorway, drop down and follow the passage to reach the dungeon, unlocking the Megaton Hammer and the Fire Medallion along the way.

Before you leave, it's worth going south across the bridge from the exit to Goron City in the Death Mountain Crater and using your Megaton Hammer on the cave entrance to get the Magic Meter upgrade from the Great Fairy Fountain within.

Sources indicate that head to the Ice Cavern, which is located in Zora Domain (or specifically, in Zora Fountain where you encountered Lord Jabu-Jabu as a child). Doing so will see you unlock the Iron Boots; make sure you grab a Blue Fire before leaving, and return to Zora Domain and use the Blue Fire on King Zora to free him and receive a Zora Tunic, which allows you to breathe underwater for an unlimited amount of time.

According to recent reports, with both the Iron Boots and Zora Tunic in hand, we have everything we need to take on the Water Temple. Play the Serenade of Water to be teleported there when ready. Completing this will see you receive the Longshot - a Hookshot upgrade - and the Water Medallion.

Before we move onto the next temple, on this island is a plaque in front of you which hints at a puzzle involving the morning sun. If you are reading this as soon as the Water Temple has wrapped, the sun should still be rising: aim for the halo with your Bow and fire an Arrow, which will see it transform into a Fire Arrow on the platform ahead.

(As an aside, provided you have completed the previous three Adult Link temples, and have unlocked Epona, you now have everything you need to take on the optional Biggoron Sword trading sequence quest.).

Recent findings suggest that when you’re ready, head to Kakariko Village as Adult Link. When you arrive, a cutscene plays showing the place on fire, Sheik appearing, and a spirit emerges from the well. You’re then taught the Nocturne of Shadow, allowing you to travel to the Shadow Temple - though there’s a place to visit you need to visit first - the Kakariko well.

As it's at the moment blocked off as an adult, you need to return as a child. If you haven’t already, learn Song of Storms from the Guru-Guru inside the windmill, then return to the windmill as Young Link and play Song of Storms back to him (now you have the Nocturne of Shadow, the return journey will be a lot quicker).

Recent findings suggest that doing so will cause the windmill to spin out of control and lower the water in the well. Drop down and complete the Bottom of the Well mini-dungeon to get the Lenses of Truth.

If you haven’t already, you also need Din’s Fire. This is acquired by visiting the Great Fairy Fountain location at the top of Death Mountain. Now you have Din’s Fire and the Lenses of Truth, play Nocturne of Shadow, then use Din’s Fire in the centre of the torches to gain access to the Shadow Temple, where you’ll get the Hover Boots along the way, and another Medallion.

Recent findings suggest that with that done, it’s time to head to Gerudo Valley. It’s found in the west of Hyrule Field, and you need either the Longshot or Epona to make it over the bridge at the start.

Complete the Gerudo Fortress stealth section - essentially let yourself get captured, then find the four carpenters so you can explore freely - then past the Mirage Desert trials (you need the Longshot and the Lenses of Truth) to reach the Evil Desert Colossus area and the Spirit Temple.

This unlocks two upcoming items - the Silver Gauntlets and the Mirror Shield - and another Medallion.

There are two optional extras in this region - a Great Fairy Fountain in Evil Desert Colossus (Nayru's Love; Bomb the cracked wall on the north side) and within Gerudo’s Fortress, the Gerudo Training Grounds (a mini-dungeon which grants the Ice Arrow).

Assuming you have now awakened every Sage and received every Medallion, it’s now time to head to the Temple of Time and start the final stretch of the game.

A cutscene will play and you’ll receive the Light Arrow, and an instruction to head to Ganon’s Castle.

Approach the lava moat around the castle to form a bridge with the help of the Sages. Now enter.

The Inside Ganondorf's Castle dungeon within is composed of six routes from a central hub, each with a 'Barrier' you must destroy; though you can tackle them in broadly any order, go for the Shadow Barrier first to get the Golden Gauntlets, which is required before tackling certain other routes in the dungeon.

Once that - and a brief trip to the Great Fairy Fountain just outside the castle beyond the bridge for a useful defensive upgrade - it’s time to scale the tower, or to halt your progress so you can mop up any remaining side-quests and collectables (see the end of this guide for a list) before the finale.

The tower within Ganondorf’s Castle is essentially a short gauntlet of battles until you reach Ganon himself at the top, and from there, it’s a linear stretch until the end credits. Good luck!

Here is a list of side quests, items and collectables you can find.

It has been revealed that nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a massive u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the organization and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors declared that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones noted during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

According to recent reports, that last bit seems likely to have been remarked with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

Industry observers note that "Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board unveiled yesterday that they're establishing a "latest standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is right now serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the organization's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has a lot of changes from the classic version of the game, but one of the chief ones is that its items are different—and while I'm only just now starting to see actual, potential game-changing bits of kit (I've gotten into trinket-juggling between pulls), there have been some pretty flavourful pieces. Like Rockslicer, an axe that lets you mine ore.

In a recent episode of the official WoW: Forever podcast, senior game designer Aidan Moon spoke a little on his design philosophies, and items that players are yet to see: "There's a lot that they have not seen that I'm very happy with and I think is a great direction for the game.".

Moon's entire philosophy seems built around flavour over form, using the example of the Ogre Loincloth, a pair of cloth casting pants with strength, as a north star of sorts: "I just want to do something different that adds texture and crunch to the game. People will see things like the Ogre Loincloth, and they'll be like: 'Why does this cloth thing have strength on it?'.

"That's because, when we say we're a fantasy-forward game, that means that before optimisation, before it being good, it needs to be flavourful, it needs to feel like it belongs in the world and that the stats are essentially a storytelling mechanism for items.".

Ultimately, Moon thinks that interesting items that are memorable are far better for the game than a purely optimal numbers upgrade: "I would rather there be an Ogre Loincloth in the game that people talk about and get upset over, than just another strength belt that people go 'oh, that's just the mail strength belt in the dungeon'.".

As for what we're yet to get to, Moon, laughing, remarks: "I've done some stupid stuff.

Sources indicate that "There may be an item that is master looter BiS—I'll just put it that way … Maybe you get extra stats if your bags are completely full." Finally. An item for people who are allergic to inventory management! Me. I'm talking about myself. My bags are so full please send help.

Feature: GTA 6 Made Me Want to Be a Good Guy (or Girl)

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (664 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m actually abiding by the traffic rules.
  • I’m playing a newly introduced GTA game but I’m clicking L3 and R3 to focus and targeting non-vitals.
  • I’m playing a fresh GTA game but I’m actually opting to defuse the situation when an NPC gets mad at me.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’m playing a new GTA game but I’m actually abiding by the traffic rules.

I’m playing a newly introduced GTA game but I’m clicking L3 and R3 to focus and targeting non-vitals.

I’m playing a fresh GTA game but I’m actually opting to defuse the situation when an NPC gets mad at me.

The more I reflect on my time with GTA 6, the more I realise this is not the GTA I necessarily grew up with, even though the carnage is always there bubbling beneath the surface.

That’s because just like GTA Vice City and GTA San Andreas, I do have the option to go on a reckless murdering spree.

I could stock up on grenades and sticky bombs and create chaos on a highway.

I could go to a beach and mow down innocent bystanders in a scene so gruesome it’d make Jack Thompson pass out.

I think this is the most remarkable thing about GTA 6 – it’s made me play differently to past titles, even though nothing has actually changed.

Industry observers note that so, why is this? Why am I choosing non-lethal as much as humanly possible, when the game allows me to go mental if I want to?

I think it’s a few reasons, personally.

Firstly, Jason and Lucia certainly aren’t saints by any stretch, but they just don’t seem like the type to go on a killing spree.

This isn’t the first GTA game to have protagonists with a slightly softer personality – GTA 4’s Niko immediately springs to mind, as does GTA 5’s Franklin.

But I think with romance being one of this game’s central themes, you really get to know these characters intimately.

It’s about the quiet moments, rubbing your partner’s feet in front of the TV.

It’s relatable – and if it’s relatable, then I think the vast, vast, vast majority of us are kind and caring to others.

Of course, this is still a video game and I racked up kills in the hundreds by the end of the campaign, but I never felt like I was doing it on purpose.

Recent findings suggest that I made mistakes – I sometimes knocked cyclists clean into the air. I wouldn’t do that in real-life. But I did try to avoid these moments as much as possible here.

Recent findings suggest that one other wrinkle is that the realistic graphics mean the violence is pretty visceral. It’s fascinating to think how much criticism the PS2 trilogy got at the time, when it looks like a cartoon compared to this game.

I wouldn’t say the violence necessarily deterred me from being a cold-blooded killer, but I can see how it would affect others.

And also it’s a gameplay mechanic, right?

Behaving recklessly and showing no real care for other virtual life will alter your criminal profile, and change how the world reacts to you.

I ended up with a personality trait sitting somewhere between saint and sinner, but I think that’s probably normal as you’re still going to have to punch an NPC in the mouth from time-to-time.

I’m sure there’ll be people who see the GTA series as more of an arcade game than the life sim it’s become in GTA 6, and there’ll be many who don’t like this change.

For me, I’m fascinated by how Rockstar subtly convinced me to play a GTA game like it’s not a GTA game. And I didn’t even really notice it until recently.

That’s just one of the title’s many, many achievements – and one of the reasons why it’s now the highest rated game of all time.

Have you found you’re playing GTA 6 in a less aggressive manner than past titles? Are you taking care on the road and picking the non-lethal option wherever possible? Be a bit nicer to the Leonida natives in the comments section below.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that as we reflect on 25 years of Super Smash Bros.
  • As highlighted by Sakurai on social media, the Switch 2 exclusive is officially one year old as of this week.
  • In a recent development, in the game director's message, he also touches on his future as a game creator.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as we reflect on 25 years of Super Smash Bros. Melee, it seems game director Masahiro Sakurai is taking a moment to remind everyone that Kirby Air Riders has now been available for a year.

As highlighted by Sakurai on social media, the Switch 2 exclusive is officially one year old as of this week. It's received multiple updates since launch and Nintendo recently rolled out the last two amiibo.

In a recent development, in the game director's message, he also touches on his future as a game creator. Here's a rough translation of this part of Sakurai's post via EventHubs: "Time flies. I wonder how much more I'll be able to make".

Sakurai admittedly isn't getting any younger, and Kirby Air Riders included "everything" at launch, so it seems this is a genuine reflection on his future as a game creator. He has reportedly claimed to be semi-retired in the past, but this eventually led to Kirby Air Riders. He's also raised his future within the game industry on multiple other occasions.

Just earlier this week at the Famitsu 40th Anniversary Festival, Sakurai apparently revisited a column he had written about retirement, and how his decision depends on the demand for his work, and if he remains capable of delivering it (via OtakuKart). He's also questioned when his "spirit" might break. For now, though, he's still apparently working at "full throttle".

If we do hear any significant updates about Sakurai's future projects, or anything else he is up to, we'll be sure to let you know.

Are you still playing Kirby Air Riders on Switch 2? What are your thoughts about Sakurai's future? Do you think he might have any surprises for fans, or do you think it's time for him to enjoy retirement? Let us know in the comments.

Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the organization's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors.
  • BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals.
  • In a recent development, build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the organization's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it says on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

In a recent development, build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Announced in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

Sources indicate that the same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The organization grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "currently engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hours before it's even playable in most of the world, Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken the record for the most viewers across livestreaming platforms like Twitch.

In a recent development, according to streaming data and analytics website Streams Charts, GTA 6 had amassed 6.38m live viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick at 12:30 UTC today. At that time, the game had been officially available for a few hours in Newly introduced Zealand, and elsewhere by using a region-switch trick.

Recent findings suggest that the previous record for most live viewers was set by Valorant, Riot Game's popular tactical shooter, during its closed beta in xx. That game brought in 1.74m live viewers, but it's worth noting there was a promotion offering players a chance to access the beta if they watched a stream. Despite having no such incentive, GTA 6 has more than tripled Valorant's record.

Industry observers note that twitch is the largest platform for GTA 6 streams according to Streams Charts, and already the game is the 6th biggest category in Twitch history. It's also expected the figure will increase as GTA 6 introduces officially in more regions of the world.

In a recent development, if you'd like to find out when exactly Grand Theft Auto 6 releases for you, check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 launch time guide for an accurate list by country. You can also read the Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 guide for a full breakdown on all the details ahead of its launch in your region.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that publisher PLAYISM and developer viv have unveiled Saihate Station: Twilight Edition, a Switch version of the 2D exploration horror adventure game including the base game and downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” as well as two mini-games. It will launch on March 25, 2027 worldwide with English, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese, and Simplified Chinese language support. A physical edition will be available in Japan for 8,800 yen.

Sources indicate that saihate Station first released for PC via Steam on March 7, 2025. The downloadable content “Twilight Railway” launched on April 18, 2025.

Here is an overview of the game, via PLAYISM:.

In a recent development, since its release in March 2025, this 2D exploration horror adventure game has recorded a cumulative series total of 1.6 million downloads, an exceptional achievement for an indie free game, and continues to receive passionate support from fans in Japan and abroad. Now it is finally coming to Nintendo Switch!

Saihate Station: Twilight Edition includes the main game, the downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” and two mini-games, all in one package.

“After falling asleep on the last train, I woke up in a bizarre place called Saihate Station…”.

In a recent development, haru Akinashi is a self-effacing office worker who lacks confidence and fails at everything he tries. Having slept through his stop on the last train, he finds himself trapped in a bizarre place called Saihate Station, where gruesome supernatural phenomena occur.

Shion Tatsunami is his complete opposite: a cheerful, talented colleague and former friend—happens to be there as well, and the two promise to work together to return home.

Their interactions are awkward at first, given the estrangement, but with each problem they overcome together, Haru recalls their former friendship, and their bond grows stronger than before.

Then, the truth of the world closes in.

In a recent development, the main game features four multiple-ending story routes. The ending branches based on fluctuations in Haru’s “dependency level,” which changes according to the player’s actions.

In a recent development, starting November 20, pre-orders for the physical edition will begin sequentially at retailers in Japan. As a first-print bonus, a “shaka-shaka acrylic stand keychain” featuring a train and character motif will be included. A limited edition featuring a special box with an “exclusive newly drawn mini-game book” and a “Haru-Shion handkerchief” is also planned. Bonuses and limited editions are available in limited quantities, so please place your pre-order early.

Guarding Stars Made A Major Change To The Book's Ending I Don't Understand

💡 Key Takeaways
